description: Dummy Tickets Submitted for Refund (Housemaids), spec v0.4. Rebuild of FXrhGBJUnGYgrs9R on the CC Non Received golden rails: secret + callback allowlist + bearer shape check, fail-closed population gate, 13 gates in ACP Order, runs log before delivery. DR

parameters.notes: ERP-COMPLIANCE: empty-exit-ok - every path out of this node either throws or returns a literal one-item array. It cannot hand back an empty stream, so it cannot be the node that strands the lease. Deliberately NOT given alwaysOutputData: if it ever did return nothing, an injected empty item would turn a loud stop into a silent one, and this node's whole job is to be loud.

ERP-COMPLIANCE: no-breaker-because a PAGINATED sweep stops itself sooner than a breaker could, and this node cannot see the batch until the walk is over. Get Dummy Ticket Transactions fetches page N+1 only after page N returns, so the FIRST failing page ends the sweep - at most one wasted call. A breaker here reads the finished walk and could only abort work that is already done. The per-item fan-out is different and does carry one: Get All-Time Refunds completes every call in its batch before any code of ours runs, so nothing else can notice ERP failing mid-batch, and Judge Refunds Batch judges it. (This sentence used to cite Get Transaction Detail and Judge Detail Batch alongside it; both were deleted on 2026-08-24 when the transaction-detail call was found never to have been a mapped route.)

ERP-COMPLIANCE: empty-exit-ok - the two ways this node has nothing to say are already ITEMS, not absences: _empty for a genuinely clean window, _seed_only when open cases must still be re-read. The final `return out` is reached only after transactions.length === 0 has been handled, so out is non-empty by construction. Deliberately NOT given alwaysOutputData: this node throws on a failed completeness gate, and injecting an empty item would turn a loud stop into a silent one.

TWO RULINGS, ONE NODE, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The second one was added on 2026-08-24 with setNodeParameter /notes, which REPLACES the field - it destroyed the first, and erp_compliance.py went from PASS to FAIL on a live flow until this was noticed. Append here; never overwrite.

parameters.content:
## 1 · Intake — the golden validator, verbatim

POST `/webhook/applicant-dummy-ticket-refund-audit`

**Manual only.** No schedule, no email — the spec says this check sends none, and production sends none. Keep it that way. The portal fires this webhook only when a person triggers the check; `Run Manually` is the other entry. There is no Schedule or Cron node in this flow.

**This path is inherited, not chosen.** The check was cut over on 2026-08-19 by adopting the retired flow's path, because the portal's own registry lives in the Security Room's Supabase project. `/webhook/dummy-tickets-housemaids` no longer exists.

The three security checks in `Validate Inputs` are **skeleton** and must not be re-derived: the `X-SR-Webhook-Secret` shared secret, the `callback_url` **origin allowlist** plus the `/ta-callback/<64-hex>` path shape, and the `Bearer <token>` shape check that stops CRLF injection into three authenticated ERP reads.

✅ **Closed 2026-08-19.** The flow this replaces (`FXrhGBJUnGYgrs9R`) had **none of the three** and was live on this very path: its webhook `options` were empty, so anyone who reached the URL could name their own `callback_url` and have the whole audit couriered to them. It is now **archived** — which both closes that exposure and stops a republish from colliding on this path and taking the portal's traffic back to the unaudited logic. This check is marked *Handles sensitive data = YES*.

**A rejection answers HTTP 200** with `accepted:false`, not a 4xx — inherited golden behaviour the portal is built against. A missing secret is rejected **silently** (`_silent`) so nobody who finds the URL can mail-bomb the team; the consequence is that a misconfigured caller looks like a run that produced nothing. Check the execution list, not the alert channel.

**One value per run.** The device id is derived from the bearer JWT's own `device` claim, so the operator supplies the token and nothing else. This flow holds **no ERP credential of its own** — it uses the caller's token, and ERP logs every read under that identity.

## 2 · Population + GATE 2 (fail-closed)

Expense **492**, windowed on the transaction `date` — never the flight, booking or refund date. Page size **200**; the spec's "caps at size 40, walk 4 pages" was measured at a different size, so the 137-row reference window is **1 page, not 4**.

**GATE 2 fails closed.** A declared `totalElements` that is null, `""` or non-numeric **aborts the run** — never coerced, never defaulted, never compared.

That exact shape is why this guard is written the way it is. The sibling CC flow had it as:
```
declared = (b.total != null) ? b.total : b.totalElements
if (collected < Number(declared)) throw
```
ERP returned `total: ""`. `"" != null` is true, `Number("")` is 0, so the test became `24000 < 0`. It truncated at 24,000 of 29,772 rows; ERP returns newest-first, so the 5,772 dropped were the **oldest**. The run reported SUCCESS and published thousands of false reds.

The flow this replaces has **no assertion here at all**.

Also asserted: every row really is expense 492. A dropped filter would audit every transaction in the window with every later gate still passing.

## 3 · Enrichment — and a measured free win

**The per-transaction detail call drops from 137 to 1 per run.** Probed 2026-08-19: **136 of 137** rows carry `Applicant ID - N` in the transaction description, and the parsed id matched `applicants[0].applicant.id` on **6 of 6** sampled rows with **zero** disagreements. The ticketing card is on the search row too (`fromBucket`), so nothing is lost by skipping it.

The ACP identity row binds this check to the detail call; the sibling *Applicant Real Ticket* row already uses this parse, for exactly this reason. **The deviation is declared, not silent.** Gate 20's policy is untouched — the id still comes from a structured source, never from a name.

`Select Unresolved` emits only the rows that still need the detail call. When none do, it re-reads the first transaction as a **sentinel**: returning zero items would skip the scorer and end the run having audited nothing, and routing round it with an IF would feed one node from two branches and **duplicate every case**. One redundant call buys a chain that cannot double-execute.

Both ERP passes are paced **5 concurrent / 500 ms** — *bursts are what got the ERP account disabled in June 2026*. The flow this replaces ran the detail sweep at **10/200**.

Applicants are chunked **25 at a time** into `0-Fetch Tickets`, which returns only the twelve fields the gates read, so the parent retains kilobytes rather than applicant trees.

**1 of 137 rows is a housemaid charge** (`transactionType HOUSEMAID`, `Maid -` prefix, resolves `housemaids[0]` not `applicants[0]`). This applicant-scoped check cannot own it, so it is counted and declared — not dropped, and not sent to a verifier who would have no question to answer. **The spec does not cover this case.**

## 4 · The 13 gates, then runs log, then delivery

Gates run in ACP `Order`; the case takes the **worst** of its tickets (Order 40) and lists every one it saw.

```
  5  population, fail-closed
 10  DUMMY only, EXACT match
 20  identity from the plural array
 30  unreachable = OUTAGE -> pending
 40  worst-of ranking
 50  not yet due -> pending
 60  refunded -> clean
 70  Lost / REFUND_FAILED -> RED
 80  Used -> verifier
 90  zero or unknown amount -> pending
100  past due / never scheduled -> RED
110  repeat bookings, threshold 2 (ADDITIVE)
115  terminal net -> pending, no_gate_matched
```

**Order 90 MUST precede 100.** Behind it, the empty-schedule default matches every unscheduled ticket and drags all **154** zero-amount `CANCELED` cases into the red — the noise floor returns.

**Gate 110 is ADDITIVE, not a verdict.** Threshold **2** (Hassan, 2026-08-19, "for now"). It routes a case to a reviewer *alongside* the money verdict, so it can surface a case whose money is clean — and it can **never** downgrade a finding. No money finding depends on it: findings and exposure are identical at every threshold. Cost at 2, month scale: **281 booking reviews against 7 findings.** Raise with `repeat_threshold`, or switch off with `repeat_bookings_off: true`.

**Runs log is written FIRST**, then the portal callback, so a failing display target cannot cost the run its record. It carries counts, totals and declared gaps only.

**Tripwire:** measured expectation is ~11 real losses. Findings above the ceiling **throw** rather than publish accusations about named people.

## Owner rulings and declared gaps — read before trusting a run

All four business questions are **SETTLED** (Hassan, 2026-08-19). Each default is a ruling, not a guess; each is overridable in `params` purely so an alternative can be *measured* before anyone changes their mind.

**1 · Blank refund schedule — FLAG IT.** A dummy ticket with no automatic refund date and the money still out is treated as *nobody scheduled a refund* and raises a red. Measured effect: **1 red across 93 applicants** — not noisy. Without it a forgotten refund would be permanently invisible to this check; the spec's own leak figure is 68 tickets / AED 194,793. Override: `empty_schedule_means_do_not_request: false`.

**2 · Zero-amount siblings — CLEAN.** A case whose money all came back reads clean even with a cancelled zero-amount ticket beside it (was *pending*, affecting 26 of 93). Two guardrails kept: a case holding **only** zero-amount tickets stays pending — nothing in it was ever verified as refunded — and the ruling can never promote a finding. Override: `immaterial_ranks_below_refunded: false`.

**3 · Repeat-booking threshold — 2, "for now".** A booking-behaviour question, not a money one, and **no finding depends on it**. ADDITIVE: it routes alongside the money verdict and never downgrades a finding. **281 booking reviews against 7 findings at month scale** — 40 reviews per finding, ruled on the 5-day number before that was known. Raise with `repeat_threshold`, or switch off with `repeat_bookings_off: true`.

**4 · Applicants only.** A charge resolving a **housemaid** rather than an applicant is out of scope — 1 of 137 rows. Counted in the run record and declared; no case created, and not sent to a verifier who would have no question to answer.

**Verifier rules 1 and 2 are BUILT** — see Note 6. Enforcement lives in `Merge Verdicts`, not the prompt.

### What is still genuinely open

**No `Used` outcome has ever appeared** — not in 93 applicants, not in 605, across 1,290 tickets read. So **gate 80 and verifier rule 1 are covered offline only. Do not record them as validated.**

**Gate 100's date-based half still has no live case.** It fires only through the blank-schedule ruling; no ticket past a real `requestRefundOn` + 30 days has been observed. Keep the gate as the guard for the day that stops being true, but never record that half as validated.

**Charges that cannot become cases.** June produced **15** rows carrying no applicant id in the description and none on the detail. One case is one applicant, so they are listed in the workbook as `needs_attribution` with their transaction ids and are **not adjudicated and not counted in any verdict total.** They need manual attribution. May produced none — this only surfaces at month scale.

**Sign-off is not done.** `Test cases verified`, `Business Validated` and `Technical Validated` are all still unticked, and the flow is live.

// One row per run. COUNTS, TOTALS AND DECLARED GAPS ONLY - no ids, no names, no per-case
// figures. This is the row someone reads in passing, so it must be safe to read in passing.
const payload = $('Build Case Payload').first().json || {};
const s = (payload.result_data && payload.result_data.summary) || {};
const pop = s.population || {};
const zar = s.zero_amount_ranking || {};
const rep = s.repeat_bookings || {};
const byV = s.by_verdict || {};

return [{ json: {
  run_id: payload.run_id,
  completed_at: s.completed_at || payload.completed_at || '',
  run_date: s.run_date || '',
  window: (s.range_start || '') + '..' + (s.range_end || ''),
  span_days: s.span_days,
  overall: s.overall || '',
  population_declared: pop.declared,
  population_pulled: pop.pulled,
  population_pages: pop.pages,
  transactions_processed: s.transactions_processed,
  housemaid_charges_out_of_scope: s.housemaid_charges_out_of_scope,
  applicant_id_via_description_parse: s.applicant_id_via_description_parse,
  applicant_id_via_detail_call: s.applicant_id_via_detail_call,
  unique_applicants: s.unique_applicants,
  applicants_scored: s.applicants_scored,
  applicants_unreachable: s.applicants_unreachable,
  findings: s.findings,
  clean: s.clean,
  pending: s.pending,
  portal_rows: s.portal_rows,
  surfaced_by_repeat_review: s.surfaced_by_repeat_review,
  exposure_total_aed: s.exposure_total_aed,
  by_verdict: JSON.stringify(byV),
  grace_days: s.grace_days,
  repeat_threshold: rep.threshold,
  immaterial_ranks_below_refunded: zar.immaterial_ranks_below_refunded,
  cases_clean_with_zero_amount_sibling: zar.cases_clean_with_zero_amount_sibling,
  cases_only_zero_amount_tickets: zar.cases_only_zero_amount_tickets,
  runs_log: s.runs_log || '',
  declared_gaps: (s.declared_gaps || []).join(' || ')
}}];

options.systemMessage:
You are an auditor's assistant on a maids.cc money-out check. A dummy flight ticket is bought purely for visa documentation and is ALWAYS supposed to be refunded. Your job is narrow: read what staff wrote and answer one question per ticket. You do not decide the case.

Return one verdict object per ticket present in the evidence.

RULE 1 - tickets under rule_1_used_tickets (someone flew on a dummy ticket).
Question: does the written record say the applicant HAD to fly on this ticket?
  EXPLAINED      - the record states a reason the travel was necessary. You MUST put the exact sentence in quoted_sentence.
  NOT_EXPLAINED  - there is a written record, but nothing in it says the travel was necessary.
  NO_TEXT        - there is no written record at all on this ticket.
  UNRESOLVED     - you cannot tell from what you were given.

RULE 2 - tickets under rule_2_finding_tickets (money went out and did not come back).
Question: does the written record CLAIM the refund was handled outside ERP?
  CLAIMED_OFF_ERP - the record names the refund. Put the exact sentence in quoted_sentence, and set amount_named / route_named to whether it states the amount and how the money came back. Put in who_must_produce_receipt whoever the record indicates should hold the receipt.
  NO_CLAIM        - there is a written record, but it makes no such claim.
  NO_TEXT         - there is no written record at all on this ticket.
  UNRESOLVED      - you cannot tell from what you were given.

HARD LIMITS - these are checked in code after you answer, so guessing gains nothing:
- Never treat the mere EXISTENCE of a note as an explanation or a claim. A note that mentions travel is evidence a note exists, not evidence the travel was sanctioned. Quote the sentence or return NOT_EXPLAINED / NO_CLAIM.
- Never infer anything from the route or the dates. A route like DMM-DXB-MNL on a dummy ticket is the normal booking pattern, not a story.
- Never treat a refund_reason value as a claim that money arrived. It records why a refund was REQUESTED, not that it was received.
- Never treat an empty all_time_refund_history as proof no refund exists. It only counts as evidence when walk_complete is true, and even then it supports NO_CLAIM, never CLAIMED_OFF_ERP.
- If the evidence is thin, say UNRESOLVED. That is a safe, expected answer. Do not stretch to be helpful: clearing a real loss is the worst outcome available to you.

parameters.content:
## 5 · The AI verifier (runs AFTER the results callback)

Reds are already visible in the portal as provisional when this starts, so a slow or failing verifier cannot delay them.

**Only the residue reaches the model.** Everything settleable from structured fields was settled by a gate. Two shapes are left: a dummy ticket someone **flew on** (rule 1), and a **finding** (rule 2).

**Grounding.** Each case carries the ticket's own written record plus an **all-time ERP refund search**. That search uses `operation: 'like'` deliberately — `contains` returns HTTP 500 on this endpoint, a wrong operator rather than a missing permission, which is why an earlier spec revision believed the call was blocked. An empty history counts as evidence **only** when the walk is proven complete (`pulled == totalElements`); that assertion travels with the bundle. **Passport numbers are stripped before anything reaches the model.**

**The prompt asks for discipline; `Merge Verdicts` imposes it.** Only two model answers may move anything, and each needs its quoted sentence present:

| model says | effect |
|---|---|
| `EXPLAINED` + quote | that **ticket** becomes `clean_explained` |
| `CLAIMED_OFF_ERP` + quote | that **ticket** becomes `unresolved` — **pending**, and the amount is kept as a claim, never written off |
| anything else, no quote, no answer, model error | **unchanged** — the gates' verdict stands |

There is **no path here by which a confirmed loss becomes clean.** `NO_TEXT` and `UNRESOLVED` are auditor review, never green.

The clean is **ticket-scoped**, then the case re-takes the worst of its REMAINING tickets — the fix for the spec recheck's severity-1, so one explained emergency can never absorb a sibling's overdue red.

nodes.name: Any verifier work?
nodes.notes: Select For Verifier returns nothing when no case needs a person's words read, which is the NORMAL outcome of a clean month. alwaysOutputData turns that absence into one empty item so this node can see it; without both halves the branch simply stops and Release ERP Lease is never reached. That is what left the lease held on execution 100409, on a run n8n marked success.

nodes.name: Mark Prior Runs Superseded
nodes.notes: D16/D9. Stamps every EARLIER run of this check for this window as superseded, so a reader summing the Runs table gets one run per window instead of five. Matches on `window` alone: this table holds only this check's runs, so no check_id discriminator is needed. Runs BEFORE Write Run Row, so every matching row is a predecessor by construction and the filter needs one equals condition and no not-equals - a condition no Data Table filter in these flows uses. SUPERSEDED MEANS ONLY 'a later run for this window exists', never that the later run was good. Matching zero rows is the normal first-run case; alwaysOutputData keeps Write Run Row reachable when that happens.

nodes.notes: D16/D9. The run record, in a store whose update can stamp many rows at once - which the Google Sheets node cannot do at this volume. This does NOT replace the Sheets append: the Run Summary tab stays the human-readable surface and is untouched, as is the Cases tab. What this adds is an answerable question - 'which run_id is current for this window' - so the Cases tab can be FILTERED rather than summed blind. Summing it blind is exactly how AED 79,774 was reported against a real 34,129. Reads $('Build Summary Row') by name rather than auto-mapping, so the stamp node in front of it cannot disturb the mapping. Numbers are coerced because several summary fields emit '' rather than 0 when a branch did not run. executeOnce because the stamp emits one item per row it updated.

nodes.name: Record Verifier Outcome
nodes.notes: D17. Runs AFTER the verifier and recomputes its outcome from Merge Verdicts' decision rows, because this flow's run summary is written before the verifier is even selected and so can never report on it. Recomputes rather than trusting __counters, which lives on the last merged item and disappears when the merge yields none.

nodes.name: Stamp Verifier Outcome On Run
nodes.notes: Updates the Runs row this execution already wrote (before the verifier ran) with the review's actual outcome. Matched on run_id alone: the row was written earlier in this same execution, so exactly one row carries this run_id.

nodes.name: Run Monthly
nodes.notes: Monthly on the 15th at 06:00 Asia/Dubai, auditing the previous full calendar month. Feeds Manual Run Config, which shapes the same envelope the webhook used to deliver, so Validate Inputs and everything referencing it are unchanged. Cannot succeed until a stored ERP credential holds a production token - ERP tokens last 24h.
